checks.check: HTTP account isolation in local demo
HTTP advertises current version
HTTP create and idempotent replay
HTTP known ID from sibling account denied
HTTP pagination across 55 actual API-created messages
HTTP public/private conversation separation
HTTP serves all JavaScript modules including mutation guard
HTTP rejects duplicate parameters and empty selectors
HTTP rejects compressed bodies rather than silently decoding unsupported input
HTTP self-revocation rejects human tokens and does not fake a missing M2M backend
HTTP authorized catalog supplies names without sibling account or private data
HTTP catalog pagination keeps two contexts distinct and creates no tickets
HTTP catalog denies forbidden filters and a cursor from another actor
HTTP server search reaches a ticket beyond the first 25 without preloading pages
HTTP combines literal query, public status and priority before pagination
HTTP filtered pagination has 30 distinct results and rejects cursor reuse with another query
HTTP search preserves account/private-note isolation and advertises the implemented capability
HTTP priority update is versioned, minimizes response and supports exact replay
HTTP stale version and changed idempotency payload do not overwrite priority
HTTP requester, sibling account and mass assignment cannot change priority
HTTP paginated timeline and real presentation module keep internal reasons out of client events
HTTP same-priority review is a no-op and capabilities announce only implemented operations
HTTP operator claims responsibility with version increment and no principal identifier in DTO
